tone_statements.citation: Stappers, Leo, L. Mulaji & T. Kalela. 1980. Textes kanyok. Africana Linguistica 8 (Annales MRAC 101): 199-226. Tervuren.
tone_statements.quote: L'absence d'un signe sur une voyelle ou sur des voyelles successives Indique qu'el le(s) porte(nt) un ton haut. L'accent grave marque un ton bas. L'accent circonflexe ou la séquence "sans signe" suîvied'un accent grave symbolise un ton descendant. Le trait vertical indique l'abaissement du ton haut par rapport au ton haut immédiatement précédent. L'accent grave flottant, enfin, marque un ton descendant postérieur et il est en distribution complémentaire avec le ton haut abaissé.
tone_statements.translation: The absence of a sign on a vowel or on successive vowels indicates that it/they bear a high tone. The grave accent marks a low tone. The circumflex, or the sequence 'no sign' followed by a grave accent, symbolises a falling tone. The vertical stroke indicates the lowering of the high tone relative to the immediately preceding high tone. The floating grave accent, finally, marks a posterior falling tone and is in complementary distribution with the lowered high tone.

sources.citation: Stappers, Leo, L. Mulaji & T. Kalela. 1980. Textes kanyok. Africana Linguistica 8 (Annales MRAC 101): 199-226. Tervuren.
sources.note: Intro pp. 201-202 (Western Kanyok, chefferie de Mulundu): vowel length contrastive, vowels before NC always long, final i/u devoiced; tone notation: unmarked = high, grave = low, circumflex = falling, vertical bar = downstepped high, floating grave = 'ton descendant postérieur'. Nothing about stress / accent d'intensité.

tone.says: Western Kanyok texts mark high, low and falling tones on every vowel, plus a lowered (downstepped) high after a high and a floating final falling tone in complementary distribution with it.

sources.quote: Ciluba also has this rule ... Preliminary evidence indicates that it is characteristic of at least two other "reversing" languages-Southern Kete and Kanyok-as well, suggesting a correlation between reversal and High Tone Lowering.
sources.note: Classes Kanyok among the Bantu 'tone reversal' languages (surface tones opposite to Proto-Bantu reconstructions, like Ciluba and Ruwund) and reports preliminary evidence that Kanyok also has the phrase-level High Tone Lowering rule (H not followed by L realized mid). No inventory or analysis of Kanyok itself.
